questions.stem: Listen to the announcement. What is the problem?
options: A signal fault is causing delays of up to an hour
A storm has closed the line to Leipzig for the day
Trains to Leipzig are leaving up to an hour early
The line to Leipzig will be closed for one hour
questions.explanation: You heard „wegen einer Signalstörung“ and „Verspätungen von bis zu einer Stunde“. „Die Störung“ is a fault, and „bis zu“ means up to.

audio.text: Wegen einer Signalstörung kommt es auf der Strecke nach Leipzig zu Verspätungen von bis zu einer Stunde.

questions.stem: Listen to the announcement. What should passengers do?
options: Buy a ticket at the airport
Take the replacement bus
Wait for the next S-Bahn
Walk to the airport
questions.explanation: You heard that the S-Bahn „fällt aus“ because of „Bauarbeiten“ (construction work), and passengers should use „den Ersatzbus“. „Ausfallen“ means the service is not running at all, so waiting would not help.

audio.text: Wegen Bauarbeiten fällt die S-Bahn zwischen Ostbahnhof und Flughafen aus. Bitte benutzen Sie den Ersatzbus.

questions.stem: Listen to the announcement in the shop. What is unusual about today?
options: The shop is closed all day
The shop closes early, at 4 pm
The shop opens late, at 4 pm
The shop stays open until 6 pm
questions.explanation: You heard „schließt heute ausnahmsweise schon um sechzehn Uhr“. „Ausnahmsweise“ means as an exception, and „schon“ signals that the time is earlier than usual.

audio.text: Liebe Kundinnen und Kunden, unser Geschäft schließt heute ausnahmsweise schon um sechzehn Uhr.

questions.stem: Listen to the voice message. What has changed?
options: Training will be at the sports ground instead of the hall
Training has moved from tomorrow to the weekend
Training will be in the hall instead of outdoors
Training is cancelled because of the weather
questions.explanation: You heard „nicht in der Halle …, sondern auf dem Sportplatz“. „Nicht … sondern“ replaces one place with the other, which is why Mia asks Jonas to bring running shoes.

audio.text: Hallo Jonas, hier ist Mia. Das Training morgen findet nicht in der Halle statt, sondern auf dem Sportplatz. Bring bitte Laufschuhe mit.

questions.stem: Listen to the weather forecast. What is expected in the afternoon?
options: Heavy thunderstorms
Dry, sunny weather
Clearing skies after rain
Light morning showers
questions.explanation: You heard „am Nachmittag muss jedoch mit kräftigen Gewittern gerechnet werden“. „Jedoch“ (however) contrasts the afternoon with the dry morning, and „mit etwas rechnen“ is to expect something.

audio.text: Am Vormittag bleibt es trocken, am Nachmittag muss jedoch mit kräftigen Gewittern gerechnet werden.

questions.stem: Listen to the news item. What did the survey find?
options: Half of all teachers feel stressed by their students
Young people feel less stressed by school than before
More than half of young people feel stressed by school
Fewer than half of young people feel stressed by school
questions.explanation: You heard „mehr als die Hälfte der Jugendlichen“ feel „durch die Schule gestresst“. „Laut einer Umfrage“ (according to a survey) introduces the source, and „mehr als“ is the detail the distractors change.

audio.text: Laut einer neuen Umfrage fühlt sich mehr als die Hälfte der Jugendlichen durch die Schule gestresst.

questions.stem: Listen. What has happened to the exhibition?
options: It has been closed since the end of March
It will open for the first time at the end of March
It has been shortened so that it ends in March
It has been extended until the end of March
questions.explanation: You heard „ist bis Ende März verlängert worden“, a perfect passive. „Verlängern“ is to extend, and „bis“ marks the new end date.

audio.text: Die Ausstellung ist bis Ende März verlängert worden.

questions.stem: Listen. When does the student discount not apply?
options: On weekdays
In the school holidays
After eight in the evening
At weekends
questions.explanation: You heard „zwanzig Prozent Ermäßigung, allerdings nicht an Wochenenden“. „Allerdings“ introduces the exception, and „die Ermäßigung“ is a discount.

audio.text: Mit Schülerausweis bekommen Sie zwanzig Prozent Ermäßigung, allerdings nicht an Wochenenden.

questions.stem: Listen to the announcement. What are passengers asked to do?
options: To hand their luggage to the staff
To leave their luggage near the exit
Not to leave their luggage unattended
To keep their luggage off the seats
questions.explanation: You heard „ihr Gepäck nicht unbeaufsichtigt zu lassen“. „Unbeaufsichtigt“ means unsupervised, and „wir bitten … zu“ is the formal way to make a request in an announcement.

audio.text: Wir bitten alle Fahrgäste, ihr Gepäck nicht unbeaufsichtigt zu lassen.

questions.stem: Listen. What happens on Friday the fifteenth?
options: The language course finishes
The language course results come out
Enrolments for the language course close
The language course begins
questions.explanation: You heard „Anmeldeschluss … ist Freitag, der fünfzehnte“. „Die Anmeldung“ is enrolment and „der Schluss“ is the end, so it is the closing date for enrolments.

audio.text: Anmeldeschluss für den Sprachkurs ist Freitag, der fünfzehnte.

questions.stem: Listen. Why is the event being called off?
options: Too many people have registered
The weather forecast is too poor
The venue has become too small
Too few people have registered
questions.explanation: You heard „wegen zu geringer Teilnehmerzahl“: the number of participants is too low. „Absagen“ is to call off, and „gering“ means small or low.

audio.text: Die Veranstaltung muss leider wegen zu geringer Teilnehmerzahl abgesagt werden.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker want help with?
options: Using the ticket machine
Finding the ticket office
Buying a ticket for a friend
Getting a refund on a ticket
questions.explanation: You heard „wie dieser Fahrkartenautomat funktioniert“. „Der Automat“ is a machine, and „würden Sie mir bitte zeigen“ is a polite request for a demonstration.

audio.text: Würden Sie mir bitte zeigen, wie dieser Fahrkartenautomat funktioniert?

questions.stem: Listen. What put the speakers off in the end?
options: The cost
Both the time and the cost
Neither the time nor the cost
The time it would take
questions.explanation: You heard „Nicht die Kosten, sondern der Zeitaufwand hat uns … abgeschreckt“. „Nicht … sondern“ rules out the cost and names the time involved as the real reason.

audio.text: Nicht die Kosten, sondern der Zeitaufwand hat uns letztlich abgeschreckt.

questions.stem: Listen. How has the speaker's feeling changed?
options: The longer they live in Berlin, the less they miss country life
The longer they live in Berlin, the more they miss country life
They have always preferred country life to living in Berlin
They miss Berlin more now that they live in the country
questions.explanation: You heard „Je länger …, desto weniger vermisse ich das Landleben“. „Weniger“ is the word to catch: 'the less', not 'the more'.

audio.text: Je länger ich in Berlin wohne, desto weniger vermisse ich das Landleben.

questions.stem: Listen. What will the speaker probably do this evening?
options: Study for the maths exam
Go to the cinema
Help a friend study for maths
Sit the maths exam
questions.explanation: You heard „Ich hätte eigentlich Lust auf Kino, aber ich muss noch … lernen“. „Hätte … Lust“ is a wish in Konjunktiv II, and „aber ich muss“ shows that the obligation wins.

audio.text: Ich hätte eigentlich Lust auf Kino, aber ich muss noch für die Matheprüfung lernen.

questions.stem: Listen. What do you learn about her?
options: She would volunteer at the shelter if she had more time
Although she has little time, she volunteers at an animal shelter
Because she has little time, she has stopped volunteering
She has a lot of free time, so she volunteers at a shelter
questions.explanation: You heard „Obwohl sie kaum Zeit hat, engagiert sie sich ehrenamtlich im Tierheim“. „Obwohl“ concedes the lack of time, and „sich engagieren“ is to get involved.

audio.text: Obwohl sie kaum Zeit hat, engagiert sie sich ehrenamtlich im Tierheim.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker decide?
options: To come along despite being tired
To stay home because of tiredness
To come along because they are not tired
To come only if they feel less tired
questions.explanation: You heard „Ich bin zwar müde, aber ich komme trotzdem mit“. „Zwar … aber“ concedes the tiredness, and „trotzdem“ (anyway) confirms the decision to go.

audio.text: Ich bin zwar müde, aber ich komme trotzdem mit.

questions.stem: Listen. What are the plans?
options: A barbecue first and then a restaurant
A restaurant, because the weather will be bad
A barbecue at a restaurant whatever the weather
A barbecue or a restaurant, depending on the weather
questions.explanation: You heard „Je nachdem, wie das Wetter wird, grillen wir oder gehen ins Restaurant“. „Je nachdem“ means depending on, so the choice is still open.

audio.text: Je nachdem, wie das Wetter wird, grillen wir oder gehen ins Restaurant.

questions.stem: Listen, then choose what it means.
options: The museum was built during the war and later destroyed
The museum is being rebuilt now that the war is over
The museum was saved from destruction during the war
The museum was destroyed in the war and later rebuilt
questions.explanation: You heard „wurde … zerstört und später wieder aufgebaut“, two passive verbs in the imperfect. „Wieder aufbauen“ is to rebuild, so the order is destruction first.

audio.text: Das Museum wurde im Krieg zerstört und später wieder aufgebaut.

questions.stem: Listen, then choose the meaning.
options: If you had told me, you would have helped me
If I had found out sooner, I would have helped you
When I found out earlier, I helped you
If I find out sooner, I will help you
questions.explanation: You heard „Wenn ich früher davon erfahren hätte, hätte ich dir geholfen“. Two „hätte“ forms make it a past condition that was not met: the speaker did not help.

audio.text: Wenn ich früher davon erfahren hätte, hätte ich dir geholfen.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say about him?
options: He is said to have founded the company on his own
He should found the company on his own
He wanted to found the company on his own
He had to found the company on his own
questions.explanation: You heard „Er soll das Unternehmen ganz allein gegründet haben“. „Sollen“ with a past infinitive passes on what others claim, so the speaker is reporting, not advising.

audio.text: Er soll das Unternehmen ganz allein gegründet haben.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the meaning.
options: I have been told the concert is sold out
I told them the concert is sold out
I was asked whether the concert is sold out
I said the concert had been sold out
questions.explanation: You heard „Mir ist gesagt worden, dass …“, a perfect passive with a dative person. The speaker is the one receiving the information, which is what „mir“ shows.

audio.text: Mir ist gesagt worden, dass das Konzert ausverkauft ist.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker need to do?
options: Lend their phone to someone
Have their phone repaired by someone
Repair their phone themselves
Leave their phone at home
questions.explanation: You heard „Ich muss mein Handy reparieren lassen“. „Lassen“ with an infinitive means having something done by someone else.

audio.text: Ich muss mein Handy reparieren lassen.

questions.stem: Listen, then choose what happened.
options: He got home late because of a phone call
The phone rang just before he left home
He had barely got home when the phone rang
He hardly ever gets home when the phone rings
questions.explanation: You heard „Kaum war er zu Hause angekommen, klingelte das Telefon“. „Kaum“ at the front with the pluperfect means 'no sooner … than', and the verb comes straight after it.

audio.text: Kaum war er zu Hause angekommen, klingelte das Telefon.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the meaning.
options: We have nothing left to wait for
We would rather not wait any longer
There is no point in waiting
We have no choice but to wait
questions.explanation: You heard „Es bleibt uns nichts anderes übrig, als zu warten“. „Übrig bleiben“ is to be left over, so nothing else is left to do but wait.

audio.text: Es bleibt uns nichts anderes übrig, als zu warten.

questions.stem: Listen, then choose what the speaker means.
options: If only I hadn't said that!
I didn't say that!
I would never say that!
Should I not have said that?
questions.explanation: You heard „Hätte ich das bloß nicht gesagt!“. Konjunktiv II with „bloß“ or „nur“ and the verb first is a wish about the past, so the speaker regrets something they did say.

audio.text: Hätte ich das bloß nicht gesagt!

questions.stem: Listen and choose the meaning.
options: She acts as if she had not heard anything
She really did not hear anything
She would like to hear nothing more
She acts as if she had heard everything
questions.explanation: You heard „Sie tut so, als hätte sie nichts gehört“. „Als“ followed directly by the verb is a short form of „als ob“, and the Konjunktiv II marks the pretence.

audio.text: Sie tut so, als hätte sie nichts gehört.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the rule?
options: The children may only watch TV once their homework is done
The children must watch TV before they do their homework
The children may watch TV while they do their homework
The children may never watch TV on a school day
questions.explanation: You heard „dürfen erst fernsehen, wenn die Hausaufgaben erledigt sind“. „Erst … wenn“ means only once, so permission depends on the homework being finished.

audio.text: Die Kinder dürfen erst fernsehen, wenn die Hausaufgaben erledigt sind.

questions.stem: Listen. How does the speaker feel?
options: Impressed
Relieved
Amused
Outraged
questions.explanation: You heard „Das ist ja wohl die Höhe!“, an idiom for 'That's the limit!'. „Die Höhe“ is literally the height, and „ja wohl“ adds indignation.

audio.text: Das ist ja wohl die Höhe!

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker expressing?
options: Sympathy for someone who is unwell
Gratitude for someone's help
Disbelief at what someone has said
Agreement with what someone has said
questions.explanation: You heard „Das kann doch nicht dein Ernst sein!“: 'You can't be serious!'. „Der Ernst“ is seriousness, and „doch“ adds emphasis to the disbelief.

audio.text: Das kann doch nicht dein Ernst sein!

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker doing?
options: Refusing to eat the food because it is cold
Complaining politely while claiming not to complain
Praising the food warmly and asking for more
Asking the cook for the recipe of the dish
questions.explanation: You heard „Ich will ja nicht meckern, aber das Essen war schon mal besser“. „Meckern“ is to grumble, and „ich will ja nicht …, aber“ is a classic way to soften a complaint.

audio.text: Ich will ja nicht meckern, aber das Essen war schon mal besser.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker's attitude?
options: They are completely confused
They don't mind either way
They strongly disagree
They are very interested
questions.explanation: You heard „Das ist mir eigentlich egal“. „Egal“ means it makes no difference, and „eigentlich“ (actually) softens the statement.

audio.text: Das ist mir eigentlich egal.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker doing?
options: Inviting someone to a party after the Abitur
Congratulating someone on passing the Abitur
Wishing someone luck before the Abitur
Consoling someone who has failed the Abitur
questions.explanation: You heard „Herzlichen Glückwunsch zum bestandenen Abitur!“. „Bestanden“ means passed, so this is congratulations after the event; good luck beforehand would be „Viel Erfolg!“.

audio.text: Herzlichen Glückwunsch zum bestandenen Abitur!

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker doing?
options: Apologising for being late
Agreeing reluctantly
Asking for a repetition
Politely disagreeing
questions.explanation: You heard „Da muss ich dir leider widersprechen“. „Widersprechen“ is to contradict, and „leider“ makes the disagreement polite.

audio.text: Da muss ich dir leider widersprechen.

questions.stem: Listen carefully. Which did you hear?
options: Es würde gebaut
Es wird gebaut
Es war gebaut
Es wurde gebaut
questions.explanation: You heard „es wurde gebaut“, the past passive: 'it was built'. „Würde“, with an umlaut, would make it conditional, and the difference is only the vowel.

audio.text: Es wurde gebaut

questions.stem: Listen. Which was said?
options: Ich hätte Zeit gehabt
Ich hätte Zeit
Ich hatte Zeit
Ich habe Zeit
questions.explanation: You heard „ich hätte Zeit“, Konjunktiv II: 'I would have time'. „Ich hatte Zeit“ is the plain past, and the umlaut is the only audible difference.

audio.text: Ich hätte Zeit

questions.stem: Listen. Which sentence did you hear?
options: Wir wären gern gekommen
Wir werden gern bleiben
Wir wären gern geblieben
Wir waren gern geblieben
questions.explanation: You heard „wir wären gern geblieben“: 'we would have liked to stay'. The umlaut in „wären“ makes it hypothetical, and „geblieben“ rather than „gekommen“ gives the verb.

audio.text: Wir wären gern geblieben

questions.stem: Listen carefully. Which was said?
options: Sie möchte es wissen
Sie müsste es wissen
Sie musste es wissen
Sie muss es wissen
questions.explanation: You heard „sie müsste es wissen“: 'she ought to know'. „Musste“ without the umlaut is the past 'had to', and „möchte“ means 'would like'.

audio.text: Sie müsste es wissen

questions.stem: Listen. Which phrase did you hear?
options: mit dem neuen Kollegen
mit den neuen Kollegen
mit dem neuen Kollege
mit der neuen Kollegin
questions.explanation: You heard „mit dem neuen Kollegen“: one male colleague, dative singular. „Kollege“ is a weak noun, so it adds „-n“; the article „dem“ rather than „den“ shows it is singular.

audio.text: mit dem neuen Kollegen

questions.stem: Listen. Which did you hear?
options: die Schüler, deren Lehrer krank ist
der Schüler, dessen Lehrer krank ist
die Schüler, denen der Lehrer hilft
die Schüler, die den Lehrer kennen
questions.explanation: You heard „die Schüler, deren Lehrer krank ist“: the students whose teacher is ill. „Deren“ is the plural genitive relative pronoun, so it refers back to „die Schüler“.

audio.text: die Schüler, deren Lehrer krank ist
